sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The petitioner who is the sole accused has filed this petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. to release him on bail in Crime No.60/2023 (Spl.Case No.60/2023) of Haliyal police station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(N) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'the POCSO Act').
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In support of his petition, the petitioner has contended that he is innocent and law abiding citizen.
He has not committed the alleged offences.
As per the complaint averments, the victim girl was in love with the accused since three years and she has voluntarily left the house.

During her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. also she has revealed that she is in love with the accused NC:
2023:KHC-D:9127 who is related to her since three years.
Absolutely, there are no material to attract the provisions of Sections 363 and 366(A) of IPC.
There is delay of 1 month 5 days in filing the complaint and the same is not properly explained.
In the absence of medical evidence, the provisions of Section 376 IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act are not attracted.
The alleged offences are not punishable either with death or imprisonment for life.
Petitioner was arrested on 14.04.2023 and since then he is in judicial custody.
He is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.
3. Learned HCGP submitted oral objections stating that the complainant Smt.Basavva is having two daughters and they are married.
She has fostered the victim girl who was aged 16 years.
Petitioner who is a distant relative of the victim girl, used to visit her house.
Such being the case, on 07.03.2023, at 4.00 p.m., the complainant realised that the victim girl was not in the house.

She NC:
2023:KHC-D:9127 searched for her everywhere and enquired her friends.
On the next day also, she searched for her.

On 09.03.2023, she came to know that the victim girl is in a NGO by name 'Sadhana' and after enquiry with Smt.Esabel, she went to Haliyal Police station and through the police, she came to know that the victim girl is in Saundatti Bal Mandir.
On the next day, she went their and met the victim girl.
However, victim girl did not speak to her properly.

Again on 31.03.2023, after coming to know that the victim girl is in Bal Mandir, Karwar, she went there and Manjunath S/O Bharamappa Pattar vs The State Of Karnataka on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166797863/

sentences.text: on enquiry, the victim girl disclosed that she is in love with the petitioner- Manjunath and that she went to his house and from there, she was sent to Saundatti police station and from there to Santavan Kendra.
Since the victim girl is aged 16 years and is a minor, the complainant lodged the complaint.
3.1. Based on the complaint, the respondent police have registered the case in Crime No.60/2023 and taken up investigation.

After conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner for the offences NC: 2023:KHC-D:9127 punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(N) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
The petitioner is arrested on 14.04.2023.

If released on bail, there is likelihood of he threatening or tampering with the prosecution witnesses and he may also delay and defeat the trial and prays to reject the petition.
4.
Heard arguments and perused the records.
5. From the complaint averments, inasmuch as the charge sheet, it is evident that the victim girl is fostered by the complainant.
Her two daughters are already married.
She was living with the victim girl.
It is stated that the petitioner is a distant relative of victim girl and from 2021-2022, she started visiting the house of the complainant and came to be acquainted with the victim girl.
On 07.03.2023, the victim girl has left the house of the complainant.
In her statement, Smt.Shambavva CW11 who is none other than the mother of the petitioner, it is stated that on 07.03.2023, the victim girl has gone to her house to stay their.
On 08.03.2023, after she enquired NC: 2023:KHC-D:9127 her, she revealed that she is in love with the petitioner.

After realising that she is a minor and the victim girl refused to return to the house of her foster mother, on 09.03.2023, she was brought to the Girl Child Welfare Centre, Saundatti and was left their.

Time to time, she was shifted to Belagavi,
Saundatti, Karwar welfare centres.
After making enquiries about her whereabouts, the complainant has gone and met the victim girl.
However, she refused to go with her and therefore she continued staying in the welfare centre.

6. After conducting detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(N) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
Since investigation is completed, custodial presence of the petitioner is not required for the purpose of investigation.
Though the offences alleged against the petitioner are non-bailable, they are not exclusively punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

The apprehension of the NC:
2023:KHC-D:9127 prosecution that he may threaten or tamper with the witnesses may be overcome by imposing stringent conditions.
For these reasons, this Court is the considered opinion that the petitioner is entitled for bail subject to conditions.

Accordingly the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Petitioner/accused is released on bail, in Crime No.60/2023 (Spl.Case No.60/2023) of Haliyal police station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(N) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, subject to following:
